newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN AIRPORTS HIT BY WAGE DEMAND ACTION.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN AIRPORTS HIT BY WAGE DEMAND ACTION.

text.p: About 3,000 aviation technicians and engineers have embarked on a work-to-rule action to press for higher wages at South African airports, a South African Airways (SAA) spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

Zelda Schuulabach said the action, which began at about eight in the morning, by members of the South African Aviation Engineering and Allied Union (SAAEAU) had caused up to 15 minute delays in domestic flights leaving Durban and Cape Town.
But major disruptions, to both domestic and international flights, were feared at Johannesburg airport which serves as the nerve centre for SAA's technical operations, she added.
"We have 3,000 technical and engineering people that have embarked on this industrial action at all our airports.
"It hasn't as yet disrupted any of our services, but we've experienced minor domestic delays," Schuulabach told Reuters.
"In Johannesburg there is a technical problem which could severely affect flights later in the day as most of our international flights are also expected to leave this evening," she added.
Schuulabach said SAAEAU had been demanding a 38 percent wage hike before declaring a dispute with SAA's management.
Union officials were unavailable for comment early on Wednesday as they were locked in talks to try to resolve the impasse, an SAAEAU officer said.
